title: Just checking

fn.en: Make enquiries; write an email of enquiry.

gr: the language of making an enquiry, and avoiding repetition

can.en: I can make a polite enquiry by phone or email and get the information I need.

acts.say: Read each one aloud and hear how polite it sounds.

sub.en: You are talking to somebody you have never met. Choose the version that works.

items.q: You are opening a formal email of enquiry.
o: I am writing to enquire about your summer courses.
I write for asking about your summer courses.
I am writing for enquire about your summer courses.

items.q: You want to know a fact, and you want to sound polite.
o: Could you tell me whether breakfast is included?
Could you tell me is breakfast included?
Could you say me if breakfast included?
items.why: After Could you tell me, the word order goes back to normal: whether/if + subject + verb.

items.q: You are asking somebody to do something for you.
o: I’d be grateful if you could send me a price list.
I’d be grateful if you can to send me a price list.
I’d be grateful you send me a price list.

items.q: You are asking on the phone, less formally.
o: I wonder if you could check for me.
I wonder if you could to check for me.
I wonder do you could check for me.

items.q: You think they may not know, and you are being careful about it.
o: Do you happen to know when it opens?
Do you happen know when it opens?
Do you happen to know when does it open?

items.q: You are closing a formal email.
o: I look forward to hearing from you.
I look forward to hear from you.
I am looking forward hear from you.
items.why: look forward to + -ing. The to here is a preposition, not part of an infinitive.

items.q: They have offered you two rooms and you want the cheaper of them.
o: I’ll take the cheaper one.
I’ll take the cheaper it.
I’ll take cheaper one.
items.why: one / ones replaces a countable noun you have already mentioned.

items.q: They ask you to fill in the form. You agree in formal English.
o: I will do so today.
I will do it so today.
I will make so today.
items.why: do so replaces a whole verb phrase and belongs to formal writing.

acts.title: To: bookings@almatytrails.kz
text: Subject: Enquiry — group walking tour, 14–16 September
I am writing to enquire about the three-day walking tour advertised on your website for September.

Could you tell me whether the price of 68,000 tenge per person includes accommodation and meals? I would also like to know whether the tour runs if fewer than six people book, as we are likely to be a group of four.
Finally, do you happen to know how difficult the second day is? Two members of our group are not experienced walkers.
I’d be grateful if you could confirm availability for 14–16 September and let me know what deposit you require.
I look forward to hearing from you.

items.r: says what the email is about before it is opened
says why the writer is writing
adds a softer, less important question
asks the reader to do something
closes the email and invites a reply

text: On the phone you can be warm and short: contractions, thanks, and a question at a time.
In a formal email to somebody you have never met, you use full forms, group your questions and sign off with Yours faithfully.

write.q: Write an email of enquiry of about 130 words. Choose one: a language course abroad, a hotel for a family trip, or a training programme at work. Follow the model: subject line → why you are writing → two main questions → one softer question → a request → close.
write.model:
Subject: Enquiry — evening English course, January intake

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to enquire about the evening English courses advertised on your website for January.

Could you tell me whether the fee of 45,000 tenge per month includes the coursebook and the placement test? I would also like to know whether classes run twice or three times a week, as I work shifts and am likely to miss one evening in four.

Finally, do you happen to know how large the groups usually are?

I’d be grateful if you could confirm which levels still have places for January and let me know what deposit you require.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Tilek

speak.q: Now make the same enquiry by phone. Say it out loud: greet, say why you are calling, ask two questions one at a time, thank them.
speak.model: Hello. I understand you run evening English courses in January? Good. Could you tell me whether the fee includes the coursebook? … Right, thank you. And do you happen to know how many people are usually in a group? … That’s helpful. I wonder if you could email me the details as well. Thank you for your help — I really appreciate it.
